minutes.headline: School building committee weighed a January instead of December town vote; no action taken, next meeting Sept 30
minutes.summary: The committee discussed how the MSBA enrollment projections were built and how to explain them to residents. The architect reviewed schematic design, roof choices, and the cost estimate and MSBA submission timeline. The chair opened discussion of a December versus January town meeting without action, and the group covered outreach, open houses, and energy and reimbursement points.

budget_items.topic: Enrollment projection used in MSBA formula
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed whether the MSBA formula used permits or local projections, and the enrollment figure was reportedly raised after re-looking at the numbers.
Two estimators are pricing the schematic design, then reconciling before the MSBA submission.
Energy-efficiency and CM-at-risk incentive points add to the base reimbursement rate; the exact rate is unknown until the MSBA meeting.
Solar does not fit in the MSBA project budget, but the design prepares for later installation, possibly via lease programs.

Public forum schedule to be drafted and circulated once the superintendent returns.

what_happened.line: The School Building Committee took no vote on whether the town vote on the school project should come in December or January; the chair opened the question for discussion only.
Two estimators are pricing the schematic design and will reconcile their estimates before the package goes to the MSBA.
Members discussed how the enrollment projection in the MSBA formula was built, and the figure was reportedly raised after the numbers were re-checked; a written clarification was requested.
The committee set a next meeting for late September to vote on the MSBA submission package, and a public forum schedule is to be drafted.
Members said solar does not fit in the MSBA project budget, and the exact reimbursement rate is unknown until the MSBA meeting.

why_it_matters: The enrollment projection and the reimbursement rate help set how much of the school project the state repays and how much falls on local taxpayers, and neither was settled at this meeting.
Residents will be asked to vote at a town meeting on the project, and the December-or-January timing decides when that vote falls and how much time the public forums have to explain the cost.
